# Explicit pytest capture parallel allowlist.
# Unlisted, unreadable, or risk-matching tests run in the serial lane.
#
# v3.66.923 -- REGENERATED FROM A WHOLE-TREE EXPERIMENT. The entire suite was
# run in ONE parallel lane on the box: 1232 files, 14,856 tests, `-n $(nproc)
# --dist loadfile`, finishing in 4m06s (user 84m29s -- about 20x). Nine tests
# failed across seven files and ZERO of them survived a serial retry, so not
# one was a real defect; all seven were lane placement. Those seven are named
# in SERIAL_EXACT_BASENAMES, not omitted here, because this file is generated
# and an omission would be regenerated away.
#
# Everything else in that run passed, and everything that passed is listed.
#
# STILL EXCLUDED, and not by heuristic: files that can EXECUTE the fallback
# runner in their own interpreter (runner_import_hazard -- static imports,
# dynamic/loader forms, monkeypatch/mock dotted paths, and loader-calls-on-
# variables in files that also name the runner). That risk has its own
# dedicated test; an entry here cannot override it. Files that only NAME the
# runner in subprocess argv, heredoc driver strings, fixture paths or
# assertion messages are reviewable like anything else -- the child process
# that executes those mutates its own interpreter and exits.
#
# WHAT THIS EVIDENCE IS NOT. It is one PACKING. xdist assigns files to workers
# by count, so another -n shuffles which files share a worker. Re-runs at
# other widths are how that gets covered, and anything they refute is a
# one-line addition to SERIAL_EXACT_BASENAMES.
